_meta.purpose: SLICE 1 seed set for the L2-RETRIEVAL eval. EXTENDS tests/lora-evals/ (run-evals.mjs + golden-set.json + rejudge.mjs + the lora_tool_decisions instrument) — it does not replace them. Where golden-set.json banks a HAND-VERIFIED expected number, every question here carries a `truth` SPEC that the runner COMPUTES from metrics_daily at run time, so the harness never trusts a number a human typed.
_meta.binds_by: clientId ONLY, never clientName — ★EVAL-BIND: two clients are named 'Influential Drones' (5bb9b2ff real, 2617b163 demo fixture) and golden-set.json binds one of them by name.
_meta.window: 2026-06-01..2026-06-30 (LAST_MONTH at time of authoring; the runner passes explicit dates, never a relative label, so the set does not rot)
_meta.coverage: 5 platforms · 10 families · high-cardinality (search_term 4,639 vals · ga_landing_page 27,299 vals) · non-additive (impression_share) · multi-level where the 4x inflation bug lived (google hour, meta age) · one question requiring >5 distinct family lookups to exercise the MAX=5 tool-turn ceiling
_meta.run_order: grouped by client so each client's cacheable prompt prefix is written once and read by the rest of its block (the LORAMER_LORA_CACHE_WARM_REORDER_V1 pattern already proven in run-evals.mjs)

questions.trait: MAX=5 TOOL-TURN CEILING — six SEQUENTIALLY DEPENDENT steps
questions.message: For June 2026, work through these in order, each answer depending on the last, and give me all six numbered: (1) which Google campaign spent the most, and how much; (2) inside THAT campaign, which ad group spent the most, and how much; (3) inside THAT ad group, which keyword spent the most, and how much; (4) inside THAT SAME ad group, which search term spent the most, and how much; (5) inside THAT SAME ad group, which device spent the most, and how much; (6) back at THAT campaign from step 1, which hour of day spent the most, and how much. Answer all six.

ceilingProbe.why_breadth_failed: The first L10 asked for six INDEPENDENT families. Anthropic can emit many tool_use blocks in ONE turn and claude-tools.ts:321 counts TURNS, not calls — so six independent lookups finished in 2 turns and the ceiling was never approached. Only a SEQUENTIAL DEPENDENCY forces turn count: step N+1 cannot be issued until step N returns. queryBreakdown exposes parentEntityId/entityId (claude-tools.ts:137) so the drill-down is genuinely serial.
ceilingProbe.expect: 6 dependent steps > MAX=5 turns. Record whether the ceiling was hit AND whether she DISCLOSED stopping early rather than silently truncating.
